A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from FlexDiT to SparseDiT. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v1 reports original image, video, and text-to-image generation experiments, component ablations, and generated samples in its main text and supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative accelerator comparisons and a training-from-scratch result in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The poolingformers, sparse-dense token modules, token recovery operations, timestep-dependent pruning, and fine-tuning initialization remain unchanged. SparseDiT is a renaming; the explicit pooling block added to Figure 2 depicts an operation already described in v1. Training from scratch is an additional evaluation of the retained architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet image generation, video generation on FaceForensics, SkyTimelapse, UCF101 and Taichi-HD, and SAM text-to-image generation. The new comparisons and initialization experiment introduce no reported dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: v2 adds quantitative comparisons against ToMeSD in Table 8 and DyDiT, TokenCache, and DiTFastAttn in Table 9. This substantially expands comparison beyond the uncompressed DiT, Latte, and PixArt-alpha models; v1's citations to ToMeSD and DyDiT did not include corresponding head-to-head results.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 adds training from scratch for 400K iterations with CFG=1.0, distinct from the retained fine-tuned image evaluation at CFG=1.5. v2 also specifies a 0.1 ToMeSD merging rate and corrects Table 1's reversed pruning interval from [0.61, 0.44] to [0.44, 0.61]. These do not establish reruns of existing experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 10 add a check of the architecture without pretrained initialization. Existing analyses of SDTM count, poolingformer count, sampler compatibility, and timestep-dependent pruning are retained, including the tables whose numbering switches between 5 and 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its performance results. The shared-seed qualitative comparisons are retained without additional seed or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 8–10 add substantial comparative and initialization results. Examples include DiT-XL ToMeSD FID 14.74 versus SparseDiT 2.38, and 512×512 DyDiT FID 2.88 with +31% speed versus SparseDiT 2.96 with +145%. Table 10 reports from-scratch FID 15.11 against a cited DiT result of 19.47 at 400K iterations. Existing Tables 1–7 retain their scores after matching renumbering. Appendix A.1 acknowledges differing source baselines for TokenCache and DiTFastAttn, limiting direct interpretation.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 3.1's formal forward/reverse diffusion definitions and AdaLN-conditioned DiT update equation. The proposed method's equations remain mathematically unchanged, with v1 Equations 2–6 becoming v2 Equations 1–5. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains spatial and temporal token sparsification that improves diffusion-transformer efficiency while preserving generation quality and supporting efficient samplers. The abstract replaces the precise 0.09 FID increase with 'similar FID,' but the introduction retains that number and the substantive claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of ToMeSD's degradation and interpretations of efficiency–quality tradeoffs against the new comparators. Appendix A.1 acknowledges differing baselines and asserts that the 0.08 FID difference from DyDiT is nearly imperceptible, without adding perceptual-study evidence. The limitation concerning manually specified architecture remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses 400K DiT-XL fine-tuning iterations and approximately 6% of training-from-scratch time; this is additional documentation, not evidence of a changed budget. It removes v1's promised code-release URL and the one-SDTM ablation's exact 6/16/6 layer allocation and use of standard bottom transformers. Latte implementation details are relocated to Appendix A.3.

R1.justification: v2 adds TokenCache, DiTFastAttn, and DiffCR references and expands distinctions from ToMeSD and DyDiT. The FiLM reference disappears with the preliminaries. These update the competitive context while retaining the original positioning around DiT-specific token reduction.

P1.justification: The paper and model are renamed, the author/affiliation block changes, and the abstract and conclusion receive localized rewriting. v2 removes the preliminaries, reorders the SDTM explanation and some ablations, moves Latte settings into the appendix, and incorporates limitations into the conclusion. Most existing prose and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column conference layout, substantially rearranges figure panels and table placement, redraws Figure 2 to show pooling explicitly, and adds Tables 8–10. The generated sample galleries retain the same images. New caption problems include Table 10 incorrectly describing a ToMeSD comparison despite containing from-scratch DiT results.

improvement.justification: v1 primarily compared with uncompressed models; v2 adds relevant accelerator tradeoffs and evidence that the architecture can train from scratch, while disclosing fine-tuning cost. These improve empirical assessability. The gain is limited by differing comparison baselines, removal of the code-release pointer and specific ablation details, and the misleading Table 10 caption.
